steps.name: A Busy Morning at Cascade Financial
steps.description: It's a busy Thursday morning. You're reviewing three client portfolios ahead of quarterly review meetings this afternoon.
steps.instructions: Click Next to continue.

steps.name: Reviewing Client Portfolios
steps.note: Client portfolio data includes PII and financial records protected under SEC and FINRA regulations. This data should never be visible to unauthorized individuals.

highlighterTexts: Three client portfolios are open on screen: Henderson, Park, and Okafor. Account balances, investment strategies, partial Social Security numbers, all visible to anyone who walks by.

steps.description: Alice opens the internal client portal to review the Henderson, Park, and Okafor accounts. She logs in and pulls up the portfolio dashboard.
steps.instructions: Log in to the Client Portal using your credentials from the password manager.

steps.name: An Urgent Phone Call
steps.description: Alice's phone rings. It's David Chen from Vennacott Capital, who handles the Henderson account. He needs the Q3 performance summary urgently for a board meeting that was moved up to this afternoon. The physical file is in the records room down the hall.
steps.instructions: Answer the phone call from David.

steps.name: Rushing to the Records Room
steps.note: Alice should have pressed Windows+L before leaving. It takes less than one second but she was in a hurry.
steps.description:
David needs that file NOW. Alice jumps up from her desk, grabbing her badge. In her rush, she completely forgets to lock her workstation. The client portfolio data for the Henderson, Park, and Okafor accounts remains fully visible on screen.

Three client portfolios. Wide open. Anyone walking by can see everything.
steps.instructions: Click Next to continue.

steps.name: Someone Stops at Your Desk
steps.note: Shoulder surfing needs no hacking skill. A phone camera captures a full screen of account data in a second, and a visitor badge gets the photographer past the front desk.
steps.description:
Alice is down the hall in the records room. A visitor walks onto the floor on his own, stops behind her empty chair and raises his phone at her screen. Henderson, Park and Okafor are all still on it.

Nobody on the floor asks who he is with.
steps.instructions: Click the visitor to read his badge, then click Next to continue.

steps.name: Gone Before She Is Back
steps.description: He lowers the phone, turns and walks off toward the lifts. The pass says he needs an escort, but nobody was with him. The whole visit took less than two minutes.
steps.instructions: Watch the visitor leave, then click Next to continue.

steps.name: Back at Your Desk
steps.description:
Alice returns with the Henderson file. Her screen is exactly as she left it, portfolios still open. Nothing on it shows that anyone stood behind her chair, so she doesn't think twice about it.

She sends David the information he needs and continues her day.
steps.instructions: Click Next to continue.

steps.name: A Normal Week Passes

email.message:
Alice,

We need to speak with you urgently regarding a security incident involving your workstation (WS-4127) on Thursday, February 13th.

Three clients, Henderson, Park, and Okafor, have reported receiving targeted phishing emails containing their exact portfolio details. Our investigation has traced the data exposure to your workstation.

Please review the incident report at security.cascadefp.com/incident-report and come to Conference Room B at 2:00 PM today. This is mandatory.

IT Security Team
email.subject: URGENT: Security Incident Requires Your Immediate Attention

steps.description: One week later. Alice is starting her Monday morning when an email from IT Security stops her cold.
steps.instructions: Read the email from IT Security.

steps.name: The Incident Report

highlighterTexts: Three clients reported targeted phishing emails with their exact portfolio details. The data exposure was traced to Alice's workstation on Thursday, February 13th. A mandatory meeting is scheduled for Conference Room B at 2:00 PM today.

steps.description: The email is devastating. Three of Alice's clients, Henderson, Park, and Okafor, reported receiving targeted phishing emails containing their exact portfolio details. The data exposure was traced to Alice's workstation.
steps.instructions: Read the highlighted email, then click the incident report link and log in.

steps.name: What Happened While You Were Gone

highlighterTexts: Visitor pass V-847, the badge you read on the man behind the chair, was detected beside your desk at 10:49. He signed in at reception and needed an escort, but no escort was logged. This was a social engineering attack.
Your workstation was unlocked for 5 minutes with three client portfolios visible. The camera footage shows what you saw: the visitor photographing your screen from behind your chair.

steps.description: The incident report pieces together the 5 minutes Alice was away from security camera footage and the badge scan log. It matches what you watched from the room: the visitor on pass V-847, standing behind her chair with his phone raised at her screen.
steps.instructions: Review the incident timeline. Pay close attention to the highlighted entries.

steps.name: The Damage

highlighterTexts: Three client accounts were compromised. The affected clients must be notified under SEC Regulation S-P. Estimated regulatory exposure is $200K+. Two clients have already requested to transfer their accounts to another firm.

steps.description: The impact assessment shows the full scope of the damage. What seemed like a harmless 5-minute absence has become a serious security incident.
steps.instructions: Review the impact assessment, then click Next to continue.

steps.name: What Should Alice Have Done?

answers.text: Asked David to wait while she saved her work
answers.explanation: The urgency of the call isn't the issue. She could have taken the call AND protected the data. Locking your screen takes less than one second.

answers.text: Pressed Windows+L to lock her screen before standing up
answers.explanation: Locking your screen takes less than one second. It should become as automatic as locking your front door. Windows+L (or Ctrl+Command+Q on Mac) protects everything at once.

answers.text: Closed the portfolio application first
answers.explanation: While closing apps helps, the fastest and most reliable protection is locking the screen (Windows+L). This protects everything at once: all open applications, files, and data.

answers.text: Taken her laptop with her to the records room
answers.explanation: Carrying your laptop everywhere isn't practical. Screen locking is the standard practice. It takes less than one second and protects all your data.

data.question: What should Alice have done before leaving her desk?

steps.instructions: Answer the question.

steps.name: Remediation: Verify Encryption
steps.note: Full-disk encryption (BitLocker on Windows, FileVault on Mac) scrambles all data on your drive. If your device is lost or stolen, the data is unreadable without your credentials. Many compliance frameworks expect it; GDPR, for example, names encryption as a security measure to consider.
steps.description:
As part of the incident response, IT Security requires Alice to verify that her workstation has full-disk encryption enabled. If her workstation had been stolen instead of just viewed, encryption would be the last line of defense.

Without encryption, anyone with physical access can read your files, even without your password.
steps.instructions: Open Settings and verify your disk encryption status. Enable it if not already active.

steps.name: Remediation: Practice Locking
steps.note: Screen locking takes less than one second. A 5-minute lapse cost Cascade Financial two clients and $200K+ in regulatory exposure.
steps.description:
IT Security requires Alice to demonstrate the screen lock procedure. This must become muscle memory: press Windows+L (or Ctrl+Command+Q on Mac) every single time you step away, even for a moment.

The 3-second rule: if you'll be away for more than 3 seconds, lock it.
steps.instructions: Lock your workstation now.

steps.name: Returning to Your Desk

data.label: A few minutes later, walking through the office...

telegramMessage.text: Hey Alice, headed to the meeting in Conference Room A. Back in 30!

steps.description:
Good, your screen is locked. Now practice the full cycle: unlock it to verify you can get back in quickly.

A little later, on her way across the office, Alice passes Jordan's desk. Their workstation is unlocked with an email client wide open. Jordan has stepped away for a meeting.

Alice now knows firsthand what can happen in just 5 minutes.
steps.instructions: Enter your PIN to unlock.

steps.name: A Colleague's Unlocked Workstation

answers.text: Leave it, it's not your responsibility
answers.explanation: Security is everyone's responsibility. You just experienced firsthand what can happen when a workstation is left unlocked for just 5 minutes.

answers.text: Lock their screen and send them a friendly private note
answers.explanation: Lock their workstation (Win+L) and send a brief, private, non-confrontational message. You're protecting them and the company, not overstepping.

answers.text: Report them to management immediately
answers.explanation: Escalating to management for a first-time lapse is disproportionate. A friendly private reminder builds better security culture than punishment.

answers.text: Post a reminder in the team chat about screen locking
answers.explanation: A public callout, even an indirect one, can embarrass your colleague. A private note is more effective and respectful.

steps.name: The Meeting with IT Security

email.message:
Alice,

Following today's meeting regarding the data exposure incident, here is a summary of outcomes and required actions:

Regulatory: Breach notices sent to the Henderson, Park, and Okafor clients under SEC Regulation S-P. FINRA review initiated.

Client Impact: Henderson and Park accounts transferring to competitor firms. Okafor account under review. Estimated revenue loss: $340K annually.

Disciplinary: Formal written warning placed in your personnel file. 90-day enhanced security monitoring.

Required Actions (immediate):
  • ✅ Full-disk encryption verified and enabled
  • ✅ Screen lock procedure demonstrated
  • Report any further suspicious activity immediately
Remember: These security habits exist to protect our clients. A momentary lapse had lasting consequences, but what you do going forward matters most.

IT Security Team
email.subject: Follow-Up: Required Actions for Incident SEC-2025-0341

highlighterTexts: The cost of a few photos: breach notices to three clients, a FINRA review and two clients moving their accounts to other firms, about $340K a year in lost revenue.
The fix is two habits you have now practiced: full-disk encryption on the device and Windows+L every time you stand up.

steps.instructions: Read the follow-up email from IT Security, then click Next to continue.

steps.name: Key Takeaways
steps.description: Congratulations on completing the Encryption & Lock Discipline training. Lock your screen every time you leave your desk. Windows+L or Ctrl+Command+Q. Make it muscle memory. The 3-second rule: if you'll be away longer than 3 seconds, lock it first. Verify full-disk encryption is enabled. BitLocker (Windows) or FileVault (Mac) ensures that stolen or lost devices don't become data breaches. Check Settings > Device encryption. Be aware of who can see your screen. Sensitive data on display is an invitation for visual hacking, from shoulder surfers, visitors, or social engineers posing as vendors. Speed is not an excuse. Locking your screen takes less than one second. The cost of not doing it can be career-altering.

description: Full disk encryption protects a device that is lost or stolen; a locked screen protects one you have only stepped away from. Learn why you need both, lock your workstation every time you leave it, and respond to a colleague's unlocked screen without making it an accusation.
